# zlaqhe

> Scales a Hermitian matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlaqhe from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlaqhe';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlaqhe( order, uplo, N, A, LDA, s, strideS, scond, amax, equed ) → Complex128Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  |  | specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the Hermitian matrix A is stored. `'upper'`: Upper triangular `'lower'`: Lower triangular. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | the order of the matrix A. |
| `A` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `max( N, 1 ) × N` |  | on entry, the Hermitian matrix A. On exit, if `equed === 'yes'`, the equilibrated matrix: diag(S) * A * diag(S). |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `A` |
| `s` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | the scale factors for A. |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `s` |
| `scond` | `number` | in |  |  | ratio of the smallest S(i) to the largest S(i). |
| `amax` | `number` | in |  |  | absolute value of largest matrix entry. |
| `equed` | `Array.<string>` | out |  |  | specifies whether or not equilibration was done. `'none'`: No equilibration. `'yes'`: Equilibration was done, i.e., A has been replaced by diag(S) * A * diag(S). |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the Hermitian matrix A is stored.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the Hermitian matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading n by n upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading n by n lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced.

  On exit, if `EQUED = 'Y'`, the equilibrated matrix: $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(S)$.
- `s`: The scale factors for A.
- `scond`: Ratio of the smallest `S(i)` to the largest `S(i)`.
- `amax`: Absolute value of largest matrix entry.
- `equed`: Specifies whether or not equilibration was done.

  -   `= 'N'`: No equilibration.
  -   `= 'Y'`: Equilibration was done, i.e., A has been replaced by $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(S)$.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `A`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlaqhe.ndarray(
    uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    s, strideS, offsetS,
    scond, amax,
    equed
) → Complex128Array
```

Equilibrates a Hermitian matrix A using the scaling factors in the vector S.

This sets A(i,j) = S(i) _ A(i,j) _ S(j) for the stored triangle. The
diagonal is forced real: A(j,j) = S(j)^2 * real(A(j,j)).

Returns the equilibration type:
- 'none' - no equilibration was needed
- 'yes' - equilibration was done

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  |  | 'upper' if upper triangle stored, 'lower' if lower |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the matrix A |
| `A` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `max( N, 1 ) × N` |  | input/output N-by-N Hermitian matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of A (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of A (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for A (in complex elements) |
| `s` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | scaling factors, length N |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for s |
| ↳ `offsetS` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for s |
| `scond` | `number` | in |  |  | ratio of smallest to largest scaling factor |
| `amax` | `number` | in |  |  | absolute value of largest matrix element |
| `equed` | `Array.<string>` | out |  |  | specifies whether or not equilibration was done. `'none'`: No equilibration. `'yes'`: Equilibration was done, i.e., A has been replaced by diag(S) * A * diag(S). |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the Hermitian matrix A is stored.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the Hermitian matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading n by n upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading n by n lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced.

  On exit, if `EQUED = 'Y'`, the equilibrated matrix: $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(S)$.
- `s`: The scale factors for A.
- `scond`: Ratio of the smallest `S(i)` to the largest `S(i)`.
- `amax`: Absolute value of largest matrix entry.
- `equed`: Specifies whether or not equilibration was done.

  -   `= 'N'`: No equilibration.
  -   `= 'Y'`: Equilibration was done, i.e., A has been replaced by $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(S)$.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `A`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zlaqhe()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLAQHE`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zlaqhe.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import zlaqhe from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlaqhe';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const s = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
const equed = [ '' ];
let out = zlaqhe( 'column-major', 'upper', N, A, N, s, 1, 1, 1, equed );
console.log( out, equed[ 0 ] );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = zlaqhe.ndarray( 'upper', N, A, N, 1, 0, s, 1, 0, 1, 1, equed );
console.log( out, equed[ 0 ] );
```

</section>
